decisionsTitle: The shop's forms get «Copiază și tradu tot»
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-10:** «On this T-shirt product page we are missing the bilingual AI translate button».

**What was wrong.** §464 put DeepL behind a one-method adapter and §482 promised one always-visible «Copiază și tradu tot: RO → EN» on every editor, greyed with the setup steps until the key is set. The shop (§683, moved to `/admin/shop` by §687) shipped without it: neither the product form nor «Cum se plătește» carried the button, and the allowlist (`translate/domain/fields.ts`) knew `titleEn` only, for «Echipa»'s boxes.

**Decision.** `TranslateAllButton` sits at the top of the product form — the «Adaugă un produs» form and each product's edit form — and of the settings form, exactly where «Echipa» places it. It takes no props: the backoffice layout's `TranslateProvider` already carries the provider's availability and the setup link (§482), so `admin/shop/page.tsx` passes nothing new. The allowlist gains `paymentEn` (with its Romanian twin `paymentRo`), a plain multi-line text, and the product's description as a rich pair, `descriptionEnBody` translated from `descriptionRoBody`; the plain `descriptionEn` stays on it for «Coduri de reducere»; `titleEn` was already on it. The server still refuses any other name (BR-REQ-060-01); the press saves nothing, and the ordinary save keeps asserting `canManageShop`.

**Who sees it.** The button is drawn where the layout offers translation — `canTranslateTexts` (§464: the Redactor, the Organizer, the Administrator, the Superadministrator) — and the shop's forms render only for who may manage the shop (`canManageShop`, §687: the Administrators by role, and any colleague holding «Gestionează magazinul»). So the Administrator and the Superadministrator get the button; a grant holder who is a Redactor or an Organizer gets it too (both predicates hold); a volunteer holding the grant does not: `canTranslateTexts` is `canEditTexts || canMessageParticipants`, which excludes a volunteer, and this change does not touch the predicate. The Organizer without the grant sees the shop read-only and gets no form, hence no button.

**Open question for the owner.** Should a volunteer holding «Gestionează magazinul» also be able to translate? It would need `canTranslateTexts` to count that grant (the translation allowance is the club's money: DeepL's free tier).

**Proof.** `tests/unit/translate/shop-button.test.ts` renders the shop's three forms in Romanian and English — «Setări»'s «Cum se plătește», the new product's form and one product's edit form (since §NNN the product's button sits at the top of «Denumirea și prețul», the first card of the product's page) — three buttons, greyed without a key, none for a role that may not; `tests/unit/translate/domain.test.ts` covers the new names and their twins.

Amends §683 (the shop's forms carry the button) and §482 (the shop is on the list of editors with «Copiază și tradu tot»).
changelogLine: - **«Copiază și tradu tot: RO → EN» on the shop's forms** — the product's title and description and «Cum se plătește» get the same one-press translate button as «Echipa»; a volunteer with the shop grant does not see it yet. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: The shop's product form (new and edit) and «Cum se plătește» carry «Copiază și tradu tot: RO → EN» in both languages, and the product's description (`descriptionEnBody` from `descriptionRoBody`, a rich text) and `paymentEn` (a plain text, with `paymentRo`) are on the translation allowlist (2026-10-10, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
